terms.name: 8 point grid
terms.definition: A spacing convention where every size and gap is a multiple of eight, so values stay whole numbers at every common screen density.

terms.name: Adaptive layout
terms.definition: A layout that switches between a few discrete arrangements chosen per size class, rather than flowing continuously as the window changes.

terms.name: App bar
terms.definition: The persistent bar across the top of an application carrying its title, navigation, and primary actions.

terms.name: Auditory icon
terms.definition: A recorded everyday sound standing for an event, so a crumple means delete by resembling the act rather than by convention learned in the interface.

terms.name: Blend mode
terms.definition: A formula for combining a layer's colour with the colour behind it, such as multiply or screen or overlay, instead of simply covering it.

terms.name: Button
terms.definition: A control that runs an action when activated, labelled with the thing it does rather than with where it goes.

terms.name: Chamfer
terms.definition: A corner cut flat at an angle instead of rounded, the sharp-edged sibling of border-radius that reads industrial, military, or sci-fi.

terms.name: Claymorphism
terms.definition: A soft style where controls look inflated from clay: pastel fills, very large corner radii, an inner highlight, and a tinted drop shadow.

terms.name: Color ramp
terms.definition: One hue rendered at a fixed series of lightness steps, numbered so that the same step means the same job in every hue.

terms.name: Comparison prevention
terms.definition: Structuring plans or products so their features and prices cannot be lined up, forcing a decision that no side-by-side reading would support.

terms.name: Container transform
terms.definition: Material's transition in which a container grows or shrinks into another one, its contents crossfading inside, so a card visibly becomes the screen it opened.

terms.name: Curb cut effect
terms.definition: The pattern where something built for a disabled minority turns out to serve everyone, the way dropped kerbs serve prams and captions serve noisy rooms.

terms.name: Deck
terms.definition: The short summary line set between a headline and the body, larger than body text and written to sell the article.

terms.name: Directionality
terms.definition: The rule that every movement carries a direction, and that using it consistently tells the reader how the parts of an interface relate.

terms.name: Drag preview
terms.definition: The semi-transparent copy of the dragged item that follows the pointer, sometimes collapsed into a stack when several items move at once.

terms.name: Easing
terms.definition: The rate of change across an animation, deciding how it accelerates and settles rather than how long it takes.

terms.name: Error identification
terms.definition: Naming the field that failed and saying what went wrong in text, rather than only outlining the input in red.

terms.name: Fake social proof
terms.definition: Manufacturing evidence that other people approve, through invented reviews, testimonials, or live activity messages nobody actually generated.

terms.name: First-line indent
terms.definition: Indenting the opening line of a paragraph so the start of each paragraph is visible without a blank line between them.

terms.name: Focus appearance
terms.definition: The size and contrast a focus indicator must reach to count as visible: enough area around the control, enough change against both the control and its background.

terms.name: Font subsetting
terms.definition: Shipping only the characters a page actually needs, cutting the font file down and letting the browser fetch ranges on demand.

terms.name: Ghost button
terms.definition: A button with no fill and often no border until you hover it, sitting at the bottom of the emphasis ladder above a plain link.

terms.name: Grunge design
terms.definition: A 1990s style of torn and photocopied texture, overlapped and cut type, off-grid layout, and dirty muted colour, where legibility is traded for emotional pitch.

terms.name: Hero
terms.definition: The large opening block of a page carrying a headline, a supporting line, imagery, and the main call to action.

terms.name: Hue
terms.definition: The attribute that gives a colour its name, red or teal or violet, expressed as an angle around a colour wheel independent of how light or vivid it is.

terms.name: Infinite scroll
terms.definition: A list that appends the next page of results automatically as the reader approaches the bottom, so the content never ends and no page controls appear.

terms.name: Inverse color
terms.definition: A surface and text pair deliberately flipped against the current theme, so a snackbar or tooltip reads as a foreign object that arrived from outside the page.

terms.name: Keyboard shortcuts dialog
terms.definition: The panel opened by pressing question mark that lists every shortcut in the application, grouped by area.

terms.name: Layout thrashing
terms.definition: Reading a geometric value after writing to the DOM in the same frame, forcing the browser to lay out synchronously over and over and stalling the animation that caused it.

terms.name: Link purpose
terms.definition: Whether a link's own text says where it goes, the reason a list of read more and click here links fails when read out of context.

terms.name: Magazine layout
terms.definition: An editorial composition with mixed column widths, one dominant lead story and smaller supporting items arranged around it.

terms.name: Menu bar
terms.definition: A permanent horizontal row of menu titles (File, Edit, View) whose menus open on click and then follow the pointer along the row.

terms.name: Mobile first
terms.definition: Designing and writing the narrow layout first and adding rules as space is gained, so the small screen is the default rather than the fallback.

terms.name: Mouse gesture
terms.definition: A command issued by the shape of a pointer stroke, usually with a button held, so a movement stands in for a menu choice.

terms.name: Neumorphism
terms.definition: A style where controls look extruded from or pressed into one background colour, shaped only by soft light and shadow.

terms.name: Onboarding checklist
terms.definition: A persistent list of setup tasks with completion state and a progress meter, kept available so the reader can return to unfinished steps.

terms.name: Outline color
terms.definition: The role that draws boundaries, split into a stronger value for edges that must be seen and a weaker one for dividers that only need to hint at structure.

terms.name: Pangram
terms.definition: A sentence that uses every letter of the alphabet at least once, used to show a whole character set in one line.

terms.name: Placeholder as label
terms.definition: The antipattern of using placeholder text as a field's only label, which vanishes on typing and usually fails both contrast and naming.

terms.name: Presentation role
terms.definition: Stripping an element of its semantics while leaving it on screen, so a table used for layout or a list used for spacing stops being announced as one.

terms.name: Pronunciation
terms.definition: How a synthetic voice says a word, and the hints an author can give when the default reading turns a product name, a units string, or a homograph into nonsense.

terms.name: Raised cap
terms.definition: An oversized opening letter that sits on the first line's baseline and rises above the text, rather than sinking into it.

terms.name: Reflow
terms.definition: The requirement that content works in one column at 320 CSS pixels wide without two dimensional scrolling, which is 400 percent zoom on a desktop.

terms.name: River
terms.definition: An accidental channel of white space running down a paragraph where word spaces on consecutive lines happen to line up.

terms.name: Scheduler
terms.definition: A grid of days crossed with hours where each event is a block in its own slot, so a week's free time is visible and an event is moved by dragging it.

terms.name: Scrollytelling
terms.definition: A narrative layout where a pinned graphic stays fixed while text scrolls past it, each step changing what the graphic shows.

terms.name: Sentence case
terms.definition: Capitalising only the first word of a label or heading, plus any proper nouns, as you would in an ordinary sentence.

terms.name: Skeleton screen
terms.definition: A loading state made of grey shapes standing where the content will be, showing the layout before the data arrives.

terms.name: Soft delete
terms.definition: Removing an item from view but keeping it recoverable in a trash or archive for a period, so deletion is reversible without a confirmation step.

terms.name: Split-flap animation
terms.definition: A digit or letter changing by flipping through every character between the old value and the new one, imitating the mechanical boards of airports and flip clocks.

terms.name: Steampunk
terms.definition: A Victorian industrial style of brass, riveted plate, wood, and leather, with gauges, cogs, and valve controls standing in for ordinary interface widgets.

terms.name: Submenu
terms.definition: A menu that opens sideways from a menu item, marked by a trailing arrow, and stays open while the pointer travels diagonally toward it.

terms.name: Synthwave
terms.definition: A neon 1980s look built on sunset gradients, glowing perspective grids, and chrome type, close to vaporwave but sincere rather than ironic.

terms.name: Text box trim
terms.definition: Cutting the leftover space above and below a line of text so the box hugs the cap height and baseline instead of the font's full ascent and descent.

terms.name: Tittle
terms.definition: The dot above a lowercase i or j.

terms.name: Tree grid
terms.definition: A table whose rows nest and expand like a tree, so hierarchy and columns of data coexist in one grid.

terms.name: Underline
terms.definition: A rule drawn under text, on the web the default marker for a link, ideally set to skip the descenders it would otherwise cross.

terms.name: View progress timeline
terms.definition: A scroll timeline measured by one element's passage through the scrollport, with named ranges for entering, being contained, covering, and exiting.

terms.name: Window size class
terms.definition: A named bucket for how much width an app window has, such as compact, medium and expanded, used in place of raw device categories.
